coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 11 units (the domain directory itself plus 10 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md) and 65 .md files totalling 1,304,173 bytes — matching the expected 11 units / 65 files exactly. Every file was read. For the six largest files (13.08.01 74k, 13.03.01 60k, 13.01.02 57k, 13.02.02 57k, 13.12 55k, 13.03.02 54k) the Deep Think Annotations sections were read at reduced line depth while Overview, Behavior, Edge Cases, States, Decisions, Open Questions and Cross-Cut Notes were read in full; no finding below rests on a Deep Think row. A programmatic scan confirmed no line in the tree is truncated mid-sentence, so no finding rests on a rendering artefact. Rubric dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 5 (Success Measurability) are marked N/A for every unit: the problem statement, constraint axes and success metrics live in meta/problem-statement.md, meta/constraints.md and vision.md, outside this domain's units, and scoring their absence here would penalise content never in scope. Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is applicable only to the domain-root unit, whose gear-marketplace-index.md Overview names Reverb (~$1B GMV), Sweetwater, eBay and Thomann, states the differentiation as a specific capability gap (provenance requires credit graph + registry + listing simultaneously) and names a defensible moat — it scores as met. Dimensions 2, 3, 7 and 8 are applicable to all 11 units. Forced inventions surfaced by implementer simulation are added as punch-list items to both the numerator and the denominator, per the scoring note that they 'count toward the ambiguity score'. Overall raw ambiguity for this domain: 14.0 points / 51 applicable checkpoints = 27.5%. The tree is of very high quality on product behaviour; the dominant defect class is not missing decisions but stale process metadata — sub-domain CX files that still assert an unresolved conflict, or defer to an ideation stage that has already run, after the owning child feature resolved it.

findings.claim: A rejected model is said to be deleted, while the same file's lifecycle diagram gives `rejected` a persistent terminal state and the file's own thesis makes every attribute's assertion chain a provenance record that must survive.
findings.evidence: 13.01.02-catalog-contribution-moderation.md:154 — "| **Contribution rejected as fabricated / not a real product** | Model is deleted. **The listing is not.** It falls back to unmatched-published (13.01.04 D-01)"  ///  13.01.02-catalog-contribution-moderation.md:64 (lifecycle diagram) — "└──────────────► rejected   └── unmerge ─┘"  ///  13.01.02-catalog-contribution-moderation.md:25 — "every attribute value on a model record carries its assertion chain (DT-08)"  ///  13.01.02-catalog-contribution-moderation.md:168 — "the **assertion survives** — \"the 1962 year range was asserted on 2026-03-04, citing [source], and confirmed by two moderators\" is a fact about the catalog, not personal data"
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must decide whether rejection hard-deletes the model row or tombstones it in state `rejected`. Choosing deletion (per the Edge Case) destroys the assertion chain that DT-08/D-10 make the feature's D-18 contribution, and leaves the lifecycle's `rejected` state unreachable. Choosing a tombstone (per the lifecycle diagram) contradicts the Edge Case's explicit 'Model is deleted'. The two choices differ in whether a repeat fabricated contribution can be detected as a repeat, and in whether the abuse audit trail exists at all.

findings.failure_scenario: A buyer adds a layaway-eligible guitar and three pedals to one cart. 13.06.01 D-06 makes the shipment the unit of quoting and D-05 makes checkout a single authorisation of the confirmed set; a layaway line has no single authorisation and a months-long hold. Implementer A silently strips the layaway line at checkout, violating D-12 ('Checkout removes only what it bought'). Implementer B blocks the whole cart. Implementer C engineers the mixed case the CX text says should be prohibited. Nothing in the domain chooses, and the CX file's own preference carries no decision number.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file flags the claim-versus-auto-settle interaction as unspecified and defers it to a stage that has run, while the domain CX file states the same rule as settled and cites a decision that does not contain it.
findings.evidence: 13.07-gear-logistics-cross-border-cx.md:52 — "Escrow must hold while a claim runs (13.07.04 Cross-Cut Notes), which collides with the order's auto-settle timer (13.06.02 D-02). A claim opened on the last day of the inspection window must suspend settlement — and therefore suspend ownership transfer (13.06.05). **Flagged for Step 5**: the interaction between claim-opening and auto-settle is unspecified and would silently transfer ownership of a destroyed object."  ///  gear-marketplace-cx.md:106 — "5. **State transition conflict**: **A claim opened on the last inspection day must suspend auto-settle** (13.06.02 D-02) and therefore ownership transfer (13.06.05), or the chain records a transfer of a destroyed object."  ///  The cited decision, 13.06.02-order-management-lifecycle.md:181, reads in full — "| D-02 | Every stall has a bounded timeout with an automatic resolution | Money plus a unique object in indefinite limbo is the worst state available. |" — and says nothing about claims suspending settlement. The nearest live rule is 13.06.02 D-15, which is scoped to *disputes*: "| D-15 | **Dispute wins on tie** with auto-settle; a dispute landing after release becomes a post-settlement claim |"
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer wiring the order state machine must decide whether opening a 13.07.04 damage claim halts the auto-settle timer. The domain CX asserts it must and cites D-02, which does not say so; the sub-domain CX says it is unspecified; D-15 covers disputes only, and 13.08 R-01 plus 13.08 D-01 establish that a damage claim is a different object from a dispute or a return. Implementer A treats a claim as a dispute and halts settlement. Implementer B does not, and a claim filed on the last inspection day settles anyway — writing an ownership transfer (13.06.05 D-05) for an object destroyed in transit, which is the exact failure gear-marketplace-cx.md CX-04 exists to prevent.

findings.claim: Two further synthesis deferrals in this sub-domain's CX file name Step 5 as the resolving stage with no owner, and neither is mirrored in any child's Open Questions.

Also open: whether the domain should actively steer irreplaceable freight items toward local pickup (13.11), which 13.07.04 DT-02 hints at and nothing currently implements."  ///  13.07-gear-logistics-cross-border-cx.md:73 — "**Synthesis questions deferred** — Low confidence. Step 5 should test whether the intersection is real enough to design for, starting with the ivory-keyed piano case."  ///  13.07.04's Open Questions are Q-01 (insurance value threshold and payer), Q-02 (resolved), Q-03 (underwrite vs broker vs carrier declared-value) — none covers a distinct freight insurance regime or freight-to-pickup steering.
findings.failure_scenario: 13.07.04 D-01 makes insurance structural above a value threshold and D-02 derives declared value from the sale price; whether freight carries its own regime rather than a larger number is left to an implementer, who will default to the single declared-value dial the file provides and silently under-protect the highest-risk shipments in the domain. No owner and an expired stage mean nothing will correct it.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file states that nothing in the sub-domain owns the remedy fork and instructs Step 5 to assign it an owner, while 13.08.01's decisions define the fork, its chooser and its failure behaviour.
findings.evidence: 13.08-returns-rma-warranty-cx.md:51 — "5. **State transition conflict**: The unresolved one. **Nothing in the sub-domain owns the remedy fork** — 13.08.01 mentions partial refund, 13.08.02 mentions repair, 13.07.04 Q-02 asks the same question from the insurance side, and no file specifies who chooses, when, or what happens if the chosen path fails. Medium confidence because the interaction is certain but the design is absent. **Step 5 must give the fork an owner.**"  ///  13.08.01-returns-refunds.md:242 — "| D-08 | **The seller offers; the buyer chooses. Replacement is not on the menu.** | Per DT-06. The remedy preference splits by persona (CX-02) — a Producer wants the repair, a Fan wants their money back — so it cannot be a platform default. The clock resumes with the time that was left"  ///  13.08.01-returns-refunds.md:237 — "| D-03 | Partial refund with retention is a first-class remedy | ... **Bounded by D-08**: it is an *offer*, and the buyer may still insist on the return. |"
findings.failure_scenario: The CX file's claim is not merely stale, it is false as written: D-08 names the chooser, D-07 names what happens if the chosen path fails, and both cite CX-02 by name. A remediation or /create-prd pass reading the CX register escalates an owned, locked design as an unowned gap, and risks a second answer that contradicts D-07's pause-never-extinguish rule — which is precisely the trap D-07 was written to close.

findings.claim: Two live behaviour questions in the sub-domain CX file carry no owner and defer to a stage that has run, and neither is mirrored in any child's Open Questions; one of them determines whether a repair voids the cover that authorised it.
findings.evidence: 13.08-returns-rma-warranty-cx.md:34 — "5. **State transition conflict**: A warranty expiring while a unit is in repair custody. Low frequency; the regime should pin at RMA issue, not re-evaluate mid-repair. `[PENDING — Step 5]`."  ///  13.08-returns-rma-warranty-cx.md:63 — "**Synthesis questions deferred** — Medium confidence. ... Step 5 should establish: does an authorised warranty repair record differently from an owner-commissioned modification, given they are the same physical act? The registry (domain 15) needs to distinguish \"manufacturer replaced this under warranty\" from \"owner had this swapped\" — the first preserves both warranty and originality standing, the second may destroy both. **That distinction is intent, not evidence**, which makes it hard to capture honestly and easy to game."  ///  13.08.02's Open Questions are Q-01 (repair-custody liability), Q-02 (off-platform repair records), Q-03 (is repair routing worth building) — none covers either.  ///  13.08.03's are Q-01 (transfer-policy data source), Q-02 (own protection plan), Q-03 (grey-market surfacing) — none covers either.  ///  The unresolved consequence is visible downstream at 13.08.03 Edge Cases — "| Manufacturer refuses because the unit was modified | A mod voids most warranties; 13.02.03 records mods | Contradiction surfaced: the registry knows about the mod the claim depends on not existing |"
findings.failure_scenario: 13.08.02 D-03 requires a repair to record what was replaced, and 13.02.03 D-03 pre-fills originality disclosure from registry history. With no warranty-versus-owner-modification distinction on the record, an implementer writes every replaced part as a modification. A manufacturer-authorised warranty repair then surfaces on the unit as an originality-destroying mod (13.02.03) and as grounds for the manufacturer to refuse the next claim (13.08.03) — the platform's own record voiding the cover it is tracking. Implementer B adds an intent flag and must invent who sets it and how it is verified, which the CX file itself notes is 'easy to game'.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the registry service record distinguishes an authorised warranty repair from an owner-commissioned modification, who asserts that distinction, and whether the warranty regime pins at RMA issue or re-evaluates mid-repair.

findings.claim: Trading in gear that carries an outstanding layaway or lien is marked with a bare `[PENDING]` that names no owner, no deferral target and no resolving mechanism, and no Open Question row in this sub-domain carries it.
findings.evidence: 13.09.01-tradein-part-exchange.md:41 — "| Owner trades in gear with an outstanding layaway or lien | They don't fully own it | `[PENDING]` — the chain (13.06.05) would know |"  ///  13.09.01's Open Questions are Q-01 (is the guide's number shown beside the trade offer), Q-02 (who pays return shipping on a rejected re-offer), Q-03 (who is the dealer) — none covers encumbrance.  ///  13.09-tradein-consignment-index.md Open Questions are Q-01 (who is the dealer) and Q-02 (does the platform act as consignee) — neither covers it.  ///  The referenced mechanism does not close it: 13.06.05-ownership-transfer-on-settlement.md:129 — "| D-01 | Settlement writes the ownership event; 15 owns the record, 13 owns the event |" records transfers but states no encumbrance semantics, and 13.06.03's layaway decisions (D-01..D-03) define the inventory hold without any trade-in interaction.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner with a guitar half-paid under a layaway agreement (13.06.03: the unit is held, ownership sits nowhere, forfeit terms are live) offers it in part-exchange. 13.09.01 D-01 requires the trade-in to write two ownership transfers. Implementer A blocks the trade-in on any encumbrance, which requires an encumbrance flag nothing defines. Implementer B allows it and writes a transfer for a unit the owner does not fully own, corrupting the very chain 13.06.05 exists to make evidential. Implementer C warns and proceeds. The text asserts only that the chain 'would know', which is a capability claim, not a behaviour.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an encumbered unit may be traded in at all, what the platform does when it detects an encumbrance, and what ownership event (if any) is written.

findings.claim: The behaviour when intake findings contradict a previous owner's disclosure recorded on the ownership chain is left `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` with no owner, and no Open Question row in the file or its siblings carries it.
findings.evidence: 13.09.03-inspection-intake-grading.md:47 — "| Findings contradict a previous owner's disclosure on the chain | The instrument's recorded history is wrong somewhere | Genuinely valuable signal; `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |"  ///  13.09.03's Open Questions are Q-01 (does the offer go up on a favourable divergence), Q-02 (is a grader's distribution surfaced), Q-03 (who performs intake grading) — none covers a chain contradiction.  ///  The adjacent, narrower case is owned: 13.02.03-modification-originality-disclosure.md:90 — "| Q-01 | When registry history contradicts a seller's disclosure, what happens — flag to buyer, flag to seller only, or block? ... | User | `/create-prd-security` |" — but that row governs a *seller's own* disclosure, not a *previous owner's* record found wrong at intake.  ///  Evidence the target stage has run: gear-marketplace-cx.md:5 — "> **Status**: [DEEP] — 13 children classified; 21 intra-domain pairs mapped and synthesised (Step 6)."
findings.failure_scenario: A bench inspection at trade-in intake finds a headstock splice that the unit's chain records a previous owner as having declared absent. The platform now holds first-party evidence that a historical record on its own append-only provenance chain is wrong. 13.06.05 D-03 forbids deletion and 13.02.04 D-03 forbids mutating sealed evidence, so an implementer must invent whether the finding appends as a contradiction annotation, whether the previous owner is notified or flagged to domain 24, and whether the chain renders the contradiction to a future buyer — decisions with reputational consequences for a party who is not on the transaction. No owner and an expired stage mean nothing collects it.

findings.claim: Whether an owner may switch between the trade-in and consignment paths after the intake grade lands is stated as unspecified with a bare preference and no owner, no deferral target and no Open Question row anywhere in the sub-domain.
findings.evidence: 13.09-tradein-consignment-cx.md:64 — "2. **Trigger chain**: Decision → intake → grade → path executes. **The grade lands *after* the choice**, which means a lowered grade changes the economics of a decision already made. Whether the owner may switch paths post-grade is unspecified and probably should be permitted."  ///  No Q row exists for it: 13.09-tradein-consignment-index.md Q-01/Q-02, 13.09.01 Q-01..Q-03, 13.09.02 Q-01..Q-03 and 13.09.03 Q-01..Q-03 contain no switching question.  ///  The paths diverge structurally, so the choice is not cosmetic: gear-marketplace-cx.md:189 — "A trade-in writes **two** transfers (13.09.01 DT-01 ...). A consignment writes **one**, consignor → buyer, the consignee never appearing as an owner because they never were one (13.09.02 D-02)."
findings.failure_scenario: An owner chooses trade-in, ships the guitar, and the intake grade comes back two grades lower, collapsing the cash offer. Under CX-03 the alternative — consignment at a higher expected net — was presented at the same decision point and is now more attractive. Implementer A permits the switch and must invent whether the consignment terms are re-agreed, whether the intake grade carries over as the custody-transfer evidence (13.09.02 Happy Path step 2), and which of the two divergent ownership-chain outcomes is written. Implementer B forbids it, so the owner's only exit is to reject the re-offer and pay to have their gear returned under the unresolved 13.09.01 Q-02. The CX file's 'probably should be permitted' is a preference with no decision number behind it.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a post-grade path switch is permitted, and if so whether the intake grade, the custody evidence and the consignment terms carry over or are re-established.
